correctness.rationale: A subset of K_{a,b,c,d} globally dominates graph and complement iff it meets each of four parts. Proper nonempty support blocks are valid and partnership means union of supports=[4]. Four explicit near-complementary support constructions give a+1,a+b,a+b+c-3,N-8 in feasible size regimes. The exhaustive upper bound by number q=0..4 of indices with one-part supported blocks handles singleton-part q=1, q=2 cross-helper blocks and q=3/4 compulsory triple supports. Independent canonical partition enumeration tested exact optimum for profiles (1,1,1,1),(2,1,1,1),(2,2,2,2),(3,2,2,2),(3,3,2,2), respectively 15,52,4140,21147,115975 partitions, all matching 2,3,4,5,6. This finite exhaustive verification corroborates the all-part upper argument.

evidence: Balanced theorem max(2q,3q-3,4q-8) covers only equal sizes; eventual theorem covers min part>=3r-6=6 for r=4, giving N-8.
Neither covers e.g (a,b,c,d)=(3,3,2,2) or all d<=5 unequal profiles.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Prior broader-r theorem has a dominating parameter restriction, not a dominating all-input conclusion.

originality.rationale: The older Anholcer et al. Proposition 6 provides the near-transversal lower bounds and complete at-most-three-part values; this is explicitly prior. The November 2 balanced four-part theorem gives the exact specialization a=b=c=d, and the November 8 large-minimum-part theorem gives N-8 for d≥6. The present all-UNEQUAL small-part classification and sharp d=1,2,3..5 boundaries are not logically implied by balanced or large-part theorems. It provides a previously unsupplied upper bound for every heterogeneous four-part profile. Full arXiv v4 could not be read; original manuscript abstract explicitly states up to three parts, residual historical risk.
residual_risks: Complete v4 original Anholcer et al. full text not materially read; novelty against a possible unpublished/disconnected four-part solution is provisional.
Finite 115,975-partition test covers at most ten vertices; unlimited profiles rely on q-class upper bound.

The exact maximum fills a specifically motivated gap in a published multipartite conjecture beyond previously solved balanced or large-size cases. Meaningful structural classification, not a parameter-table recomputation.
